abstract: This study examines the impact of generative AI on worker productivity using data from 5,179 customer support agents who received staggered access to an AI-based conversational assistant. The authors find that AI assistance increased overall productivity by 14%, with substantially larger gains of 34% for novice and low-skilled workers but minimal impact on experienced workers. The results suggest AI disseminates best practices, accelerates learning curves for newer workers, improves customer sentiment, and increases employee retention.
keyFindings: AI assistance increased productivity by 14% on average, measured by issues resolved per hour.
Novice and low-skilled workers experienced a 34% productivity improvement with AI access, while experienced and highly skilled workers saw minimal impact.
AI assistance improved customer sentiment and increased employee retention.
The AI model appears to disseminate best practices of more able workers and helps newer workers move down the experience curve.
Results demonstrate large heterogeneity in AI effects across different worker skill levels.
methodology: Staggered introduction study of a generative AI-based conversational assistant using data from 5,179 customer support agents. Productivity measured by issues resolved per hour. Analysis includes examination of customer sentiment and employee retention outcomes. Study period: April 2023 (initial issue date) with revisions through November 2023.
qualifiers: The authors provide 'suggestive evidence' regarding worker learning and skill development. The study focuses on customer support agents in a specific work domain, which may limit generalizability to other occupations. Results show large heterogeneity across workers, indicating effects may not be uniform across different workforce compositions.
